decisions.reason: As a niche but adjacent reusable crate for agriculture, it is still an early-stage option and the firm is likely to keep it on the market another year to learn more despite its lower website prominence.
A foldable large container fits the firm’s core industrial packaging business well, and a dedicated page suggests enough initial commitment to justify keeping the option open.
The stackable plastic crate is close to the established product base, so management would likely tolerate another year of uncertainty before abandoning it even if early signals are modest.
This pallet variant is a relatively low-cost extension of existing capabilities, so the firm would probably keep it available while market feedback continues to develop.
The spill-retention pallet has a clear functional use case and dedicated web presentation, which points to a stronger case for continuing the product rather than dropping it quickly.
A plastic pallet with load retainers is highly consistent with the company’s reusable logistics portfolio, and the firm would likely preserve this option while demand uncertainty resolves.
